headline: Daily Market Snapshot – June 22, 2026
summary: Key market levels for June 22, 2026. S&P 500 last closed at 7,500.58 with Monday futures slightly negative; Nikkei 225 hit an all-time record of 72,584. WTI oil fell to $75.30 on Iran deal progress; BTC near $64,197.

headline: US Stock Market Today: Live Updates 22.06.2026 – Futures Slip on Iran Talk Caution
summary: US equity futures were little changed to slightly negative Monday as investors assessed continued Iran-US nuclear talks and awaited May PCE inflation data due June 25. S&P 500 futures -0.2%, Nasdaq-100 near flat, Dow futures -29 points (-0.1%).

headline: SpaceX IPO makes history as largest ever; SPCX gains 19% on first day, closes at $161
summary: SpaceX priced its IPO at $135/share on June 11, raising $75 billion in the largest IPO in history. Shares opened at $150 and closed at $161.11 on debut day June 12, a 19.3% gain, valuing the company at $2.1 trillion. Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire based on his stake.
key_facts: Raised $75 billion, largest IPO in history
Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire

headline: SpaceX acquires AI coding startup Cursor (Anysphere) for $60 billion in all-stock deal days after IPO
summary: SpaceX announced June 16 it would acquire Anysphere, maker of AI coding tool Cursor, in a $60 billion all-stock transaction just four days after completing its record IPO. The deal raised immediate concerns about dilution for post-IPO shareholders, sending SPCX shares sharply lower.
key_facts: Deal announced just 4 days after June 12 IPO
Immediate dilution risk for post-IPO buyers
Cursor AI coding tool has large developer user base

headline: SpaceX Stock Plunge Wipes Out $620 Billion After Cursor Deal Spooks Investors
summary: SpaceX shares fell more than 6% in a two-day slide after the $60 billion Cursor acquisition was announced, erasing roughly $620 billion from the company's market value and pulling it down to $2.37 trillion from a $2.99 trillion peak. Shares are still about 31% above the $135 IPO price.
key_facts: SPCX fell >6% in two-day post-Cursor selloff
Market cap fell from $2.99T peak to $2.37T
Morningstar lowered fair value to $62 from $63

headline: SpaceX (SPCX) falls more than 3% in premarket Monday, on pace for third straight daily decline
summary: SpaceX shares fell more than 3% in premarket trading on Monday, June 22, extending a three-day losing streak following the Cursor acquisition announcement. The stock remains above its $135 IPO price but is well below its peak near $225.

headline: CFRA initiates SpaceX with Sell rating and $115 price target, citing elevated valuation
summary: CFRA initiated coverage of SpaceX (SPCX) with a Sell rating and a $115 12-month price target, substantially below the post-IPO trading price, citing the company's extremely ambitious growth strategy, elevated valuation expectations, and significant capital intensity.
key_facts: Cites elevated valuation, capital intensity, ambitious growth strategy

headline: Oil prices fall, stocks rally as US and Iran sign MOU framework to end war
summary: The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding on June 18 to end their conflict, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz and removing the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Stock markets rallied while oil prices tumbled more than 5% on prospects of normalized Iranian oil supply.
key_facts: US naval blockade of Iranian ports to be removed
Japan Nikkei soared 5.5%, South Korea Kospi +5.7%
US crude oil futures fell 4.77% to $80.83

headline: Dow climbs more than 450 points to record close as oil tumbles on potential Iran deal
summary: US stocks surged to record highs on June 14 as the US and Iran announced a potential framework deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Dow gained more than 450 points while oil prices sank sharply as investors priced in a recovery of Iranian oil exports.
key_facts: Dow climbed >450 points to record close
Oil fell sharply on Iran deal prospect
Geopolitical risk premium in energy markets fell

headline: WTI crude oil falls to $75.30 Monday morning as US-Iran nuclear talks show further progress
summary: WTI crude fell 0.73% to $75.30/barrel and Brent dropped 1.7% to $79.22 in early Monday trading, reflecting ongoing diplomatic progress in US-Iran nuclear negotiations that have significantly reduced geopolitical supply risk since the MOU signing on June 18.
key_facts: Oil down ~8% over the past week
US-Iran talks reducing geopolitical supply premium

headline: Energy stocks tumble as oil falls 5% on US-Iran deal reopening Strait of Hormuz
summary: US energy stocks declined sharply as oil prices plunged 5% following news of the US-Iran agreement. APA and Devon Energy fell more than 3.5%, Marathon Petroleum and EOG Resources dropped 3%, while Chevron and ExxonMobil lost more than 2.5% each.

headline: Fed holds rates at 3.50–3.75%, Warsh delivers hawkish surprise at first FOMC meeting as chair
summary: The Federal Reserve held the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.50%–3.75% at Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as chair, the fourth consecutive hold. Nine of 18 participants now project a 2026 rate hike; the committee removed prior language signaling rate cuts, and the policy statement was significantly shortened. Wall Street turned lower on the news.
key_facts: Median dot moved to 3.8% end-2026 vs 3.4% in March
Easing bias language removed from statement
Warsh did not submit his own rate projection
S&P 500 -0.6%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Dow -160 pts on decision day

headline: 2-year Treasury yield keeps rising after Warsh's hawkish Fed debut; 10Y dips
summary: Treasury yields showed mixed movement after the June 17 FOMC meeting: the 2-year yield rose more than 1bp to 4.179%, tracking short-term rate expectations higher after the hawkish surprise, while the 10-year yield dipped 1bp to 4.453% and the 30-year fell 2bp to 4.90%.
key_facts: Hawkish Warsh stance lifted short-term rate expectations

headline: US Dollar Index DXY holds near 100.79, supported by hawkish Fed signals
summary: The US Dollar Index DXY fell slightly to 100.7852 on June 19, but remains near a one-year high, supported by the Fed's hawkish June FOMC stance and expectations that roughly half of FOMC members project at least one 2026 rate hike. The dollar has strengthened 1.71% over the past month.
key_facts: Supported by hawkish Warsh Fed signals

headline: Gold near $4,150/oz, weekly low, as hawkish Fed and strong dollar weigh on bullion
summary: Gold fell to around $4,150/oz by June 22, its lowest since June 11, as the US dollar climbed to a one-year high following the Fed's hawkish June FOMC meeting. Nine FOMC members projecting a 2026 rate hike dampened demand for non-yielding gold. Silver's pivot was near $64.63/oz.
key_facts: Hawkish Fed and strong USD pressuring gold

headline: Bitcoin holds near $64,197 on June 22 as market sentiment remains cautious
summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,197 on the morning of June 22, with a 24-hour volume of $9.93 billion. Sentiment indicators remain cautious, with RSI at 37.90 and 18 of 30 technical signals bearish. BTC has shed roughly 30% year-to-date as institutional flows stabilized after a 13-day ETF outflow streak ended June 5.
key_facts: US spot BTC ETF 13-day outflow streak ended June 5 after $4.4B net outflows

headline: Ethereum (ETH) trades near $1,722, recovering gradually after early-2026 selloff
summary: Ethereum was trading around $1,722 on June 22, 2026, expected to range between $1,650 and $1,950 during the month. ETH experienced significant downside in early 2026 amid recession fears and selling by Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin, but has found tentative support.
key_facts: Vitalik Buterin selling pressured ETH in early 2026

headline: Japan's Nikkei 225 hits all-time record high of 72,584 on June 22, 2026
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 index surged 1.55% to a fresh all-time record of 72,584 on Monday June 22, driven by optimism around the US-Iran MOU, relief from Middle East geopolitical risk, and continued AI-driven global equity gains. South Korea's Kospi also gained 0.7% to 9,114.

headline: Bank of Japan holds rate at 0.75%, signals any move to 1.0% depends on sustained wage growth
summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its short-term policy rate at 0.75% at its June 15–16 meeting, targeting the overnight call rate around 0.75%. Policymakers signaled a move toward 1.0% will require sustained wage growth, durable inflation above target, and stable financial conditions.
key_facts: Next hike to 1.0% conditional on wage growth and inflation durability
Fed hawkish stance supporting USD vs JPY
Treasury yields elevated, weighing on gold and risk assets

headline: ECB maintains overnight rate at 2.25%, signals pause amid Middle East headwinds
summary: The ECB Governing Council held its overnight rate target at 2.25% at its June 10 meeting, continuing a policy pause that began earlier in the year. The ECB noted persistent global headwinds from Middle East tensions and US trade friction weighing on sentiment and supply chains.
key_facts: Middle East tensions and US trade friction cited as headwinds
Asymmetric risks could slow foreign demand

headline: Micron Technology (MU) shares rise 3% premarket ahead of fiscal Q3 2026 earnings due June 24
summary: Micron Technology shares climbed 3.04% to $1,168.46 in premarket trading June 22 as investors positioned ahead of its fiscal Q3 2026 earnings report on June 24. Analysts expect EPS of $19.95–$20.57 and revenue of ~$35 billion, above Micron's own guidance midpoint of $33.5 billion.
key_facts: Consensus revenue estimate: ~$35B vs guidance $33.5B midpoint

headline: FedEx (FDX) Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings due Tuesday June 23 after market close
summary: FedEx is scheduled to report fiscal Q4 2026 earnings after Tuesday's close, coming at a pivotal moment following the successful spinoff of its FedEx Freight division. Analysts expect EPS of $5.91 and revenue of $24.18 billion, with the spinoff shifting the company's financial profile heading into fiscal 2027.
key_facts: FDX Q4 FY2026 earnings due June 23 after close
FedEx Freight spun off into independent public company
Financial profile shifted ahead of FY2027

headline: Nuvalent shares surge 39% after GSK agrees to acquire cancer drugmaker for $10.6 billion
summary: GSK announced June 9 it would acquire Nuvalent, a Boston-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, in an all-cash deal valued at $10.6 billion ($124/share, a 40% premium). The deal adds two late-stage next-generation ALK/ROS1 lung cancer inhibitors with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations and is GSK's third major acquisition in the first half of 2026.
key_facts: Adds zidesamtinib (NVL-520) and neladalkib (NVL-655) ALK/ROS1 lung cancer inhibitors
Both have FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations

headline: Salesforce to acquire AI customer service platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for $3.6 billion
summary: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement June 15 to acquire Fin, formerly Intercom, for approximately $3.6 billion, adding more than 30,000 business customers and an AI agent that resolves ~76% of support requests without human intervention. The deal complements Salesforce's Agentforce platform and is expected to close in Q4 FY2027.
key_facts: Fin AI agent resolves 76% of support requests autonomously
Deal expected to close Q4 FY2027

headline: Yum! Brands sells Pizza Hut to LongRange Capital and Yum China for $2.7 billion
summary: Yum! Brands entered definitive agreements to sell Pizza Hut in two separate transactions totaling $2.7 billion. LongRange Capital will acquire Pizza Hut ex-China for approximately $1.5 billion, while Yum China will acquire Pizza Hut China for approximately $1.2 billion. Transactions are expected to close in Q3 2026.
key_facts: Yum! Brands sells Pizza Hut for $2.7B total
Pizza Hut ex-China to LongRange Capital for ~$1.5B
Pizza Hut China to Yum China for ~$1.2B
Sale follows strategic review that began November 2025

headline: Olin and Huntsman announce all-stock merger of equals to create $12B+ North American chemicals leader OlinHuntsman
summary: Olin Corporation and Huntsman Corporation agreed June 16 to combine in an all-stock merger of equals valued at approximately $2.43 billion, creating OlinHuntsman Corporation with pro forma revenues exceeding $12 billion. Olin shareholders will own ~54.5% of the combined company; more than $400 million in synergies are targeted, with deal closure expected in H1 2027.
key_facts: All-stock merger of equals valued at ~$2.43B
Ken Lane as CEO, Peter Huntsman as non-exec Chairman

headline: Ingredion to acquire Tate & Lyle in recommended all-cash deal valued at $3.6 billion
summary: Ingredion Incorporated announced on June 8 a recommended all-cash acquisition of UK food ingredients company Tate & Lyle PLC for £2.7 billion ($3.6 billion). The combined entity will be valued at approximately $9.9 billion and will focus on specialty ingredients for texture, sugar reduction, and fortification. Deal expected to close in H2 2027.
key_facts: Ingredion acquires Tate & Lyle for £2.7B ($3.6B) all-cash
Focus on specialty ingredients: texture, sugar reduction, fortification
Strategic fit with GLP-1 weight-loss drug trend (fibre/nutrients)
Deal to close H2 2027 pending regulatory approval

headline: Devon Energy completes $58B Coterra merger, targets 1.38 Mboe/d combined production in 2026
summary: Devon Energy completed its transformative merger with Coterra Energy in May–June 2026, creating one of the largest US shale operators with pro forma production guidance of 1.38 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2026, including 500,000 barrels of oil per day. The combined company plans $4.9 billion capex in 2026 and aims to return 70% of free cash flow to shareholders.
key_facts: Up to 70% of FCF returned to shareholders

headline: Telecom companies to acquire Patrick Drahi's SFR for $23.5 billion
summary: A consortium of telecom companies agreed in early June 2026 to buy SFR, the French mobile and broadband operator owned by billionaire Patrick Drahi, for $23.5 billion. The deal is one of the largest European telecom transactions of the year.
key_facts: SFR sold for $23.5B to telecom consortium
One of largest European telecom deals of 2026

headline: Nvidia announces PC chips at Computex, CEO Huang aims to reinvent PC alongside Microsoft
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced at Taiwan's Computex conference that Nvidia, alongside Microsoft, would produce new PC chips, directly challenging AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm in the personal computer market. Shares of AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm fell on the news, while Nvidia stock rose.
key_facts: Nvidia entering PC chip market alongside Microsoft
AMD, Intel, Qualcomm fell on competitive threat
Extends Nvidia's AI stack vertical integration strategy

headline: Nvidia (NVDA) rated Strong Buy by 62 analysts with average $298.93 price target, +42% upside
summary: Nvidia maintains a Strong Buy consensus from 62 analysts, with an average 12-month price target of $298.93, representing approximately 41.88% upside from current trading levels. The company's Vera Rubin architecture and data center AI dominance underpin bullish sentiment, though AMD and Broadcom are increasingly competitive.
key_facts: AMD and Broadcom gaining share in AI chip market

headline: SK Hynix surpasses Samsung Electronics as South Korea's largest listed company on AI memory boom
summary: SK Hynix surpassed Samsung Electronics in market capitalization to become South Korea's largest listed company, driven by explosive demand for its high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI accelerators. The 2026 HBM market is estimated at $54.6 billion, a 58% year-over-year increase, with supply fully booked.
key_facts: SK Hynix surpasses Samsung as Korea's largest listed company
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang visited Korea, signed multi-year HBM4 agreement with SK Hynix
Samsung scaling +50% monthly HBM capacity in 2026

headline: Microsoft trading at $379.40, nearly 20% below 52-week high; Apple near 52-week high at $311
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) has fallen nearly 20% year-to-date and trades at $379.40 on June 22, well below its 52-week high of $555. Apple (AAPL) is trading closer to its 52-week high of $311.40 and has received additional investor attention ahead of the CEO transition to John Ternus on September 1.
key_facts: 48 analysts rate MSFT Strong Buy with 32%-62% upside targets

headline: Apple names John Ternus as CEO to succeed Tim Cook, effective September 1, 2026
summary: Apple announced on April 20 that hardware engineering SVP John Ternus will become CEO effective September 1, 2026, replacing Tim Cook who will become Executive Chairman. Ternus, 51, has led hardware engineering since joining in 2001 and oversaw all major Apple hardware products including the Mac-to-Apple Silicon transition.
key_facts: John Ternus named Apple CEO effective September 1, 2026
Oversaw Mac-to-Apple Silicon transition, all iPhone/iPad lines
Board approved unanimously, succession planning well advanced

headline: Definium Therapeutics (DFTX) to present Phase 3 EMERGE topline results for MDD on June 22
summary: Definium Therapeutics hosted a live webcast at 8am EDT June 22 to discuss topline results from its EMERGE Phase 3 study evaluating a single dose of DT120 ODT 100µg in adults with major depressive disorder. The readout is a key catalyst for the company's psychedelic-derived depression therapy pipeline.
key_facts: Definium EMERGE Phase 3 topline results presented June 22
Evaluates DT120 ODT 100µg in major depressive disorder
Definium also dosed first patient in ASCEND (second Phase 3 trial)
ASCEND: 175 participants, primary endpoint MADRS at Week 6

headline: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics announces Week 52 Phase 3 VELA results for sonelokimab in hidradenitis suppurativa
summary: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics announced Week 52 results from its Phase 3 VELA program evaluating sonelokimab in hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) on June 22, coinciding with an investor day. The results mark a pivotal regulatory data package for the company's lead IL-17A/F nanobody.
key_facts: VELA Phase 3 Week 52 results for sonelokimab announced June 22

headline: Core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% YoY in April; May data due June 25, closely watched by Fed
summary: The core PCE price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge — rose 3.3% year-over-year in April 2026, up from 3.2% in March. Headline PCE rose 3.8% in April. The May reading is due June 25 and will be closely scrutinized after the Fed's hawkish June FOMC surprise.
key_facts: Core PCE 3.3% YoY in April 2026 (up from 3.2% March)
Hawkish Fed projecting rate hike if inflation persists

headline: Wall Street analyst actions: LMND and ALGN upgraded; DraftKings and Eli Lilly downgraded
summary: Recent Wall Street analyst actions include upgrades for Lemonade (LMND) and Align Technology (ALGN), while DraftKings (DKNG) and Eli Lilly (LLY) received downgrades. AI infrastructure and mega-cap platforms continue to attract price target hikes across Nvidia, Microsoft, Broadcom, and Meta.
key_facts: AI infrastructure stocks: Nvidia, Broadcom, Meta getting price target hikes
TD Cowen raises Cohu target from $60 to $80 (Buy maintained)
TD Cowen downgrades Domo from Buy to Hold, target $6 to $3.25

headline: Top analyst upgrades June 2026: AI and infrastructure platforms lead Wall Street buy-list
summary: Wall Street analysts have been actively raising price targets on AI and infrastructure mega-caps in June 2026, including Microsoft, Broadcom, Meta Platforms, and Nvidia. The upgrades reflect analyst confidence in AI-driven revenue growth and data center buildout continuing through 2026 and 2027.
key_facts: Microsoft, Broadcom, Meta, Nvidia receiving price target upgrades in June
AI infrastructure positioning drives bullish analyst sentiment
Overall: 49 upgrades, 69 downgrades in latest analyst survey
Tech sector AI capex spend underpinning consensus

headline: ExxonMobil and Chevron warn oil prices could skyrocket in coming weeks as stockpiles drain
summary: Executives at ExxonMobil and Chevron warned in late May that oil prices could surge significantly over the following months as global oil inventories continued to drain at an accelerated pace. This backdrop preceded the US-Iran peace MOU of June 18, which subsequently reversed oil's trajectory sharply lower.
key_facts: Chevron dividend yield 3.7%, 39 consecutive annual increases
Both warned of oil price surge potential pre-Iran deal
Context: Iran deal reversed outlook dramatically

headline: GSK's $10.6B Nuvalent buy is its third major acquisition in first half of 2026, bolstering oncology pipeline
summary: GSK has been aggressively expanding its oncology portfolio in 2026, with the $10.6 billion Nuvalent acquisition being its third major deal since late January. The deal adds a platform in NSCLC lung cancer treatment, including zidesamtinib and neladalkib with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations, and NVL-330 a HER2 inhibitor in Phase 1.
key_facts: GSK's third major deal of H1 2026
Total M&A spend substantially elevated in 2026
Adds NVL-330 (HER2 inhibitor, Phase 1) for NSCLC
FDA target action date for zidesamtinib: Sept 18, 2026
FDA target action date for neladalkib: Nov 27, 2026
Nuvalent NSCLC drugs already in NDA review

headline: HBM-led AI memory supercycle: 2026 HBM market forecast at $54.6 billion, up 58% YoY
summary: SK Hynix and industry analysts project the 2026 global HBM market will reach $54.6 billion, a 58% year-over-year increase, as AI accelerator demand drives an unprecedented memory supercycle. Both SK Hynix and Samsung have raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 and are expanding capacity aggressively.
key_facts: HBM3E prices hiked ~20% by SK Hynix and Samsung
AI memory shortages may last until 2027+
Customers reserving supply years in advance
Nvidia certifying HBM4 from all three major memory makers

headline: Micron Q2 FY2026: Revenue $23.86B, GAAP net income $13.79B ($12.07 EPS), AI demand surges
summary: Micron Technology reported fiscal Q2 2026 revenue of $23.86 billion and GAAP net income of $13.79 billion ($12.07/diluted share). Non-GAAP EPS was $12.20. The company guided fiscal Q3 to record revenue of $33.5B±$0.75B, gross margin ~81%, and non-GAAP EPS of $19.15±$0.40, all driven by explosive AI memory demand.
